title: Saint Francis (4 October)
hookLine: the day animals are brought to church for blessing
tomorrow: Our Lady of the Rosary (7 October)

cards: On or near the fourth of October, parish parking lots fill up with dogs on leashes, cats in carriers, a hamster in a shoebox, sometimes a horse, a goat, a goldfish in a bowl, and now and then a very patient iguana.
A priest walks down the line with holy water and blesses each one. It's noisy and a little chaotic, and people who haven't been to church in years show up.
The man behind it all died centuries ago, and near the end of his life, nearly blind and in pain, he wrote a song.

teach.h: A RICH MAN'S SON GIVES IT ALL UP.
teach.b: Francis of Assisi was the son of a rich cloth merchant, and he wanted to be a knight.
Instead, after illness and a stint as a prisoner of war, he gave it all up, stripping off even his clothes before the bishop and his father.
He lived in poverty, rebuilding ruined churches, caring for lepers, preaching peace. Others came to share that life, and then more.

teach.h: BIRDS AND A WOLF: STORIES TOLD.
teach.b: The animal stories are well-known: preaching to the birds, making peace with a wolf that terrified the town of Gubbio. Those come from collections written after his death, and people tell them as stories.
But the song is his own.
Sick and almost blind, staying at San Damiano, he wrote the Canticle of the Creatures, not in Latin but in the everyday Italian of Umbria.

It begins Laudato si', mi' Signore, praised be you, my Lord, and praises God through creation, calling each part family: brother sun, who brings the day; sister moon and the stars; brother wind; sister water, useful and humble and precious and pure; brother fire; and our sister, mother earth.
Near his death he added one more verse, for sister death. The idea is older than Francis.

teach.h: ALL YE WORKS OF THE LORD, BLESS THE LORD.
teach.b: In the Book of Daniel, in the Catholic Bible, three young men in a furnace sing, in the Douay-Rheims: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord." What Francis added was the family. Not resources, not scenery: kin.
In 2015 a pope who took his name borrowed the first line for a letter on care for the earth.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saint Francis of Assisi on 4 October, and many parishes hold a blessing of animals on or near the day; Franciscans celebrate it as a solemnity.

the poor man of Assisi who sang of creation

games.q: you're Francis near the end of your life: sick, nearly blind, in pain, staying at San Damiano. what do you write?
o: a letter of complaint about your treatment.
a song praising God through brother sun and sister water.
games.why: he wrote the Canticle of the Creatures, calling the sun, moon, wind, water, fire and earth his family.

practice: If you have a pet, sit beside it and rest a hand on it; if not, watch a bird at the window, a dog across the street, even an ant on the sidewalk, or picture an animal you've loved. Watch it breathe, alive the way you are.
If you pray, ask God to bless it; if you don't, wish it well, as kin.

wordCard.voice: Saint Francis. Francis of Assisi, the poor man who called the sun his brother and the earth his sister. His feast is the fourth of October. Today's word.

orig.note: Umbrian Italian, a daughter of Latin: brother sun, from the Canticle of the Creatures.

carryVoice: Your line: brother sun. In Francis's song, even the sun is part of the family. Until tomorrow.
